key_insight: High-speed video time-of-arrival data can be used to predict positive-phase blast duration and impulse without relying on pressure gauges.
engineering_relevance: This provides a cheaper, safer, and more deployable way to characterize blast loading for post-event analysis and explosive testing.
method: Extract time-of-arrival versus distance from high-speed video.
Fit/validate predictive models for positive-phase duration and impulse for spherical free-air bursts.
Compare model outputs against published experimental datasets for multiple ideal explosives.
evidence_signal: Across PE4, PE7, Composition B, and PETN datasets, the models achieved 5.3% mean absolute percentage error for both duration and impulse, with strong coverage of reported confidence intervals.
watch_item: The approach is validated for spherical, non-cased, free-air bursts of ideal explosives, so broader field conditions may require additional calibration or extension.
paper_title: A Novel Methodology for Evaluating Positive Phase Blast Wave Loading Parameters Using High Speed Video
